key_insight: GraphVid makes video generation easier to control by letting users specify relationships between objects with a graph, instead of relying on vague text prompts or hard-to-draw trajectories. This gives more precise multi-object control, especially in scenes with interaction, overlap, or occlusion.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of controlling multiple objects in generated videos using text or trajectory-based inputs, which become ambiguous and impractical as scene complexity increases.
method: Uses a graph-based control representation to define object identities and their interactions.
Maps graph structure into video generation guidance for more precise multi-subject motion and coordination.
Designed to handle complex scenes where objects may overlap, occlude each other, or interact in ways that are hard to describe with simple tracks.
impact: GraphVid could make controllable video generation more usable for creators and researchers by replacing fragile motion sketches with a clearer and more scalable control format. This may improve precision in editing, animation, and synthetic data generation workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of text prompt vs trajectory control vs graph control
A node-and-edge graph showing object relationships and motion constraints
A video frame sequence illustrating multi-object interaction under occlusion
An icon set for objects, arrows, and control inputs to show the workflow
paper_authors: Vedant Shah, Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Kiet Nguyen, Tianjio Yu
